clue.text: All dispersed here in living quarters

definitions.text: All dispersed here in living quarters

parts.words: All dispersed here in living quarters
parts.note: put 'All' in front and the phrase means scattered everywhere; on its own it is where a shopkeeper lives, upstairs from the business

explanation.surface: Everyone has scattered from this place where people live.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet: 'all ___' is an idiom for dispersed, and the bare phrase names lodging above a business premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers traditionally lived in rooms above their premises, so the phrase names that kind of home; with 'all' before it, it is an idiom for scattered.

clue.text: Part of TV to let off steam?

explanation.surface: A bit of television equipment is somehow a way to vent anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Old television sets used vacuum tubes, and a safety device of the same name on a boiler releases excess pressure.

clue.text: Whale or sea-monster reported in choppy Ural

indicators.note: in tells us one set of letters goes inside the other
choppy, like a rough sea, says the letters of Ural are tossed into a new order
reported means the word is heard, so we write something that sounds like it

parts.note: an orc is a mythical sea-monster, also an old name for a killer whale

explanation.surface: A whale, or perhaps some monster, has been sighted in rough water on the Ural river.
explanation.walkthrough: An orc is a mythical sea-beast, said aloud as ORQ. 'choppy' gives RUAL from URAL; 'in' sets the sound after its R. The 'or' merely joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rorqual is a baleen whale of the family that includes the blue whale and the fin whale.

clue.text: Hawker stuck with her in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests something disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A street seller is stuck with a woman who is in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' jumbles STUCK and HER together.
explanation.definitionFit: A huckster is a pedlar or street seller, someone who goes about selling small goods.

clue.text: Second student leaving port has a dance

indicators.note: leaving says one letter goes out of the word for the port

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England
L for learner, the student; here the second of the two Ls in the port's name

explanation.surface: A second pupil quits the harbour town and dances.
explanation.walkthrough: HULL is an English port on the Humber; 'leaving' drops its second L, the 'student' (L for learner), giving HUL, and 'has' adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: The hula is a traditional Hawaiian dance with swaying hips.

clue.text: Exert force on employee who is a reporter

parts.note: to press something is to push on it
a man is a worker, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Lean on the staff member who writes for the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressman is a journalist, someone who works for the newspapers.

clue.text: Left sailor with one old penny

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
and means together with
D was the symbol for a penny in Britain's pre-decimal coinage

explanation.surface: A seaman was left with a single coin from the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for a penny in old British money, before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Left in the sense of deserted or forsaken, as with a stranded ship.

clue.text: Exactly where to press

explanation.surface: Precisely the spot to push.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely or punctually; read literally it is the spot on a control to push.

clue.text: Did not finish dressing bird

indicators.note: says the word for dressing stops short of its last letter

parts.note: robing is putting on clothes, especially formal robes

explanation.surface: Someone did not finish getting dressed, like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did not finish' drops the last letter, G, from ROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a familiar garden songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: Warning everybody about including telephone service

parts.note: an alarm is a warning signal
C stands for circa, Latin for about
all means everyone

explanation.surface: An alert for everyone about something that involves the phone company.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, about, and comes before ALL; 'including' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels and phone companies offer a wake-up ring at a booked time, a service for sleepers.

clue.text: Ban this rum drink

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Prohibit this strong spirit!
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a drink but means strange: it jumbles BAN THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, once banned in many countries.

clue.text: Revolutionary beat included was not attractive

indicators.note: included says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: red is the colour of revolution, a communist
a pulse is a regular beat

explanation.surface: A rebel who kept time was not appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a verb for defeat, but it is a heartbeat; 'included' sets it inside the communist colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsed here is the opposite of attracted, as one magnet pushes another away.

clue.text: Cheaper price for dieter?

parts.note: a discounted ticket, also read as the smaller meals someone slimming must eat

explanation.definitionFit: A discounted ticket price; read literally, fare is food, and a slimmer eats less of it.

clue.text: Light twinkler?

parts.note: a star that shines in daylight hours rather than at night, the sun or the morning planet

explanation.definitionFit: A poetic name for the sun, or for the morning star, which shines when it is light.

clue.text: A mob, misguided, going round grave for explosive device

indicators.note: going round says the jumbled letters surround the next piece
misguided means led astray, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

explanation.surface: A rioting crowd surrounds a burial place to plant a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' gives A + OMB from A MOB; 'going round' wraps those letters about the burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear weapon powered by fission is the classic example of such a device.

clue.text: I had put back pounds at plant

indicators.note: put back says the letters are written in reverse order

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
L is the symbol for a pound, and LL for pounds

explanation.surface: I had returned some money at the nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns I'D into DI; L for pound, from Latin libra, doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery herb used to flavour fish and pickles.

clue.text: Partying? Or working?

explanation.surface: Is one out celebrating, or hard at work?
explanation.walkthrough: Partying is read as backing Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically, joining the Labour political party; in plain English, toiling or working hard.

clue.text: Chap coming from first half of volcanic island group

indicators.note: only the first half of the island name is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a remote cluster of volcanic islands in the South Atlantic, a British territory named after a Portuguese explorer

explanation.surface: A man arrives from a remote South Atlantic archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: Tristan da Cunha is a British South Atlantic territory; 'first half of' keeps its first seven of fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, as in the knight of the Arthurian legend who loved Isolde.

clue.text: Not much evidence that one has been crying

definitions.text: Not much evidence that one has been crying

parts.words: Not much evidence that one has been crying
parts.note: a small drop left on the cheek after weeping, a tiny sign of tears

explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed from the eye, a small sign of weeping.

clue.text: It's polluted in a channel islands sewer

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off France
a drain carries waste water, like a sewer

explanation.surface: Something is fouled in a sewer on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey, are abbreviated CI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain made acidic by industrial emissions is a classic form of pollution.

clue.text: Censor lady for the most part

indicators.note: most but not all of the name is kept: the last letter goes

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman who largely acts as censor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter, H, from EDITH.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to cut or revise text before release, as a censor does.

clue.text: Move gently when some increase offensive

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Go carefully when some escalate the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'when' into the definition; it only joins, as 'Move gently' alone gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken or relax, reducing speed or pressure.

clue.text: Say nothing to Iowa fellow included who had abnormal self-confidence

indicators.note: included says one piece is set inside the others

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
O is zero, nothing
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Keep quiet to the chap from Iowa, an overconfident fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: IA is a US postal code, Iowa; 'included' sets the fellow inside, after EG and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive preoccupation with oneself, an inflated sense of one's own importance.

clue.text: Again plan flag but leave out first name

indicators.note: leave out says a letter is removed from the flag

parts.note: the Red Ensign is the flag of British merchant ships

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: N stands for name; the first of the two Ns in the flag goes

explanation.surface: Design the flag afresh but drop the first name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Ensign is the British merchant navy flag; 'leave out' drops its first N.
explanation.definitionFit: To design something anew is to plan it over again.

clue.text: Seed-corn?

parts.note: both halves of the hyphenated word name the same thing, a single kernel of a cereal

explanation.definitionFit: A kernel of wheat or other cereal; both seed and corn are names for it.

clue.text: One colour seen in mist or on hearth

indicators.note: seen in says the pieces appear inside the word for mist

parts.note: fog is a thick mist
I is the Roman numeral for one
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A single colour glimpsed in mist or on a fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' sets the numeral and the colour within the mist. The definition is cryptic: the thing found on a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, the metal stand that holds logs in an open fireplace.

clue.text: Regular attendant is an energetic person

explanation.surface: Someone who always turns up is full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchgoer or theatregoer attends regularly; someone lively and active is also called this.

clue.text: A lot can go wrong shaped like this?

indicators.note: wrong suggests something going awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plenty may go wrong with something of this shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' jumbles A LOT CAN GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eight sides, as a stop sign is.

clue.text: Sharon dominated part of musical work

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sharon took over part of a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a composition whose main theme keeps returning, often the last movement of a sonata.

clue.text: Leaving car in good condition. It doesn't pay the motorist to get this!

definitions.text: It doesn't pay the motorist to get this!

parts.note: parking is leaving a car somewhere
fine means in good health

explanation.surface: Leaving the car in good shape; drivers hate getting this.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'pay': a motorist does pay this, but it never pays to get one.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty charge for leaving a vehicle where it should not be.
